hints: Calculate the normal reaction $R$ perpendicular to the plane with $T = 15\text{ N}$, then find the maximum available friction $F_{\text{max}} = \mu R$ using $\mu = 0.8$.
Calculate the net force tending to move the block up the plane before friction acts: $T\cos 20^\circ - mg\sin 30^\circ$.
Compare the net upward pulling force with the maximum available friction to determine whether the block will move up the plane.
walkthrough:
Calculate the normal contact force $R$ perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$R = 2g\cos 30^\circ - 15\sin 20^\circ = 20\cos 30^\circ - 15\sin 20^\circ$$
$$R \approx 17.3205 - 5.1303 = 12.1902\text{ N}$$

Calculate the maximum limiting friction available:
$$F_{\text{max}} = \mu R = 0.8 \times 12.1902 \approx 9.7521\text{ N}$$

Find the net force acting up the plane before friction opposes motion:
$$F_{\text{net, up}} = 15\cos 20^\circ - 2g\sin 30^\circ = 14.0954 - 10 = 4.0954\text{ N}$$

Compare the net force up the plane with maximum limiting friction:
$$4.0954\text{ N} < 9.7521\text{ N}\quad (F_{\text{net, up}} < F_{\text{max}})$$
$$\text{Because the net upward force is less than maximum friction, the block does not move up the plane.}$$

teacher_walkthrough: State the approach: to test whether the block moves up the plane, we calculate the net upward force pulling the block and compare it with the maximum limiting friction the rough surface can provide.

First, resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane to determine the normal reaction force $R$:
$$R + T\sin 20^\circ = mg\cos 30^\circ$$
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ - T\sin 20^\circ$$

Calculate the maximum limiting friction force $F_{\text{max}}$ using the given coefficient $\mu = 0.8$:
$$F_{\text{max}} = \mu R = 0.8 \times 12.1902 = 9.7522\text{ N}$$

Next, calculate the net force acting up the plane before friction acts (tension component up the plane minus weight component down the plane):
$$F_{\text{up}} = T\cos 20^\circ - mg\sin 30^\circ$$
$$T\cos 20^\circ = 15 \times 0.939693 = 14.0954\text{ N}$$
$$mg\sin 30^\circ = (2)(10)(0.5) = 10\text{ N}$$
$$F_{\text{up}} = 14.0954 - 10 = 4.0954\text{ N}$$

Compare the two values:
$$4.0954\text{ N} < 9.7522\text{ N}$$
$$\text{Because the net upward force }(4.10\text{ N})\text{ is less than the maximum limiting friction }(9.75\text{ N}),\text{ friction prevents any motion, so } B \text{ will not move up the plane.}$$
